credit.instrument: Long-Term Issuer Default Rating (IDR) & Senior Unsecured bonds
credit.rationale: Fitch upgraded JSW Steel's Long-Term IDR and bond ratings to BB+ from BB and removed them from Rating Watch Positive, with a Positive Outlook (release dated 05-06 Jul 2026). | RWP resolution followed receipt of proceeds (INR294bn in Mar-2026 + INR79bn in Jun-2026) from selling steel assets to the JSW-JFE Kalinga Steel 50:50 JV. | Upgrade reflects Fitch's expectation that EBITDA net leverage (incl. proportionate consolidation of the JV) will remain below its negative-sensitivity threshold.

bull_bear.body: Deleveraging via ₹37,000cr BPSL JV with JFE Steel; ₹15,000–16,000cr FY26 capex focused on growth and green steel; ₹575cr raised in JSW One funding round; dividend policy not disclosed; strong liquidity (₹16,737cr cash); sustainability-linked bonds issued; focus on debt reduction to maintain <1.75x Net Debt/Equity
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Coking coal price volatility; INR depreciation impacting FX costs; global steel demand slowdown; China export surplus suppressing prices; capex execution delays (e.g., Utkal, Dolvi); regulatory delays in mining; labor cost inflation; geopolitical risks in overseas operations; transition risks in green steel tech deployment
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and forward-looking; emphasized operational excellence, deleveraging via JV, and green steel leadership; highlighted digitalisation (Vision.AI) as key to cost and safety gains; expressed strong conviction in India’s steel demand growth and export resilience; tone was upbeat on FY26 guidance and FY31 capacity targets
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: JSW Steel’s BPSL JV effectively transfers ₹37,000cr debt to a 50:50 JV entity, improving balance sheet without equity dilution; JSW One’s ₹1,306cr credit GMV indicates successful financial services monetisation beyond steel; 30% stake in Illawarra coal mine secures long-term coking coal supply; digital AI platform (Vision.AI) projected to save ₹100cr/year across plants; 61% VASP sales mix is among highest globally for integrated producers
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net debt to equity improved significantly to 0.42x and net debt to EBITDA to 1.46x, following the JSW JFE JV deleveraging.
- Credit ratings were upgraded by Fitch (BB to BB+, Positive Outlook) and CARE (AA to AA+), reflecting improved financial metrics.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- India is in a nation-building phase with steel demand growth outpacing real GDP, and JSW aims to be the key beneficiary as the #2 producer and consumer globally.
- Strategic priorities focus on creating shared value through cost leadership, value-added products, digitalisation, and sustainability.

business.body:
- [JV Transaction] The steel business of Bhushan Power and Steel (BPSL) was transferred to the 50:50 JSW JFE Steel JV, de-consolidated from JSW Steel from 27 March 2026.
- [New JV] A greenfield 6mtpa integrated steel plant JV with POSCO was announced in Dhenkanal, Odisha, for high-grade flat steel.

latest_quarter.body: Adjusted EBITDA margin: 14.4% (Q3FY26); cost pressure from higher coking coal (QoQ), partially offset by lower thermal coal and power costs; FX loss of ₹124cr due to INR depreciation; Indian operations EBITDA margin improved to 15.0% (Adj.); US and Italy margins improved YoY
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: FY26 consolidated crude steel production guidance: 30.5mt; sales guidance: 29.2mt. Capex spend expected at ₹15,000–16,000cr for FY26.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Utkal: 5mtpa Phase-I (commissioning FY30), expandable to 13.2mtpa; Vijayanagar: 5mtpa brownfield expansion; BPSL JV: 10mtpa by 2030; Kadapa: 4mt green steel in 2 phases; EAF expansion at Kadapa; 5.5mt expansion potential at BPSL; selective M&A; 0.2mtpa Tinplate & 0.36mtpa CGL at Rajpura (FY28); 1mtpa EAF at Kadapa (FY29)
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: JSW Steel delivered record sales and EBITDA in Q3FY26 driven by 14% YoY volume growth and 61% VASP penetration, while accelerating deleveraging via a ₹37,000cr JV with JFE Steel and scaling green steel capex; the company is on track to reach 50mtpa capacity by FY31 with superior margins and digital-led cost efficiency.

open.item: Fourth coke oven battery (4 x 0.75mtpa) at Vijayanagar to be commissioned by end of FY26.
Expect to spend Rs 15,000-16,000 crore of capex during FY26.
Vijayanagar BF-3 upgradation (adding 1.5mtpa), under planned shutdown since end-Sep 2025, expected to be commissioned by end of Q4 FY26.
50:50 BPSL JV with JFE Steel (equity value Rs 31,500 cr; JFE investing Rs 15,750 cr for 50%) will enable deleveraging of ~Rs 37,000 crore for JSW Steel; transaction expected completed by Q3 FY27.
30mtpa slurry pipeline (302km) and 30mtpa Jatadhar Port for Utkal to be commissioned by FY27.
Dolvi Phase-III expansion from 10 to 15mtpa (long lead items ordered) to be completed by Sep'27.
Two pellet plants (8mtpa each) at Utkal to be commissioned by FY28.
Vijayanagar 0.4mtpa CGL by June 2028 and 0.55mtpa CRNO plant by March 2028; Khopoli 0.6mtpa CRM and 0.86mtpa CGL by Q1 FY28.
Kadapa 1mtpa EAF & section mill and Raigarh 1mtpa structural mill both to be commissioned by FY29; Rajpura Tinplate+CGL by FY28.
Targets 19% reduction in specific energy consumption to 5.65 Gcal/tcs and 39% reduction in specific water consumption to 2.21 m3/tcs by FY30.
Target 42% reduction of CO2 emission intensity to 1.95 tCO2/tcs by FY30 (from 2005 baseline), aligned with India's NDCs.
JSW Utkal Steel integrated plant Phase-I of 5mtpa (capex Rs 31,600 crore) at Jagatsinghpur, Odisha, to be commissioned by FY30.
BPSL JV (JSW Sambalpur) plan to expand to 10mtpa by 2030, from current 4.5mtpa.
Growth path to reach 50mtpa steel capacity in India by FY31 (excluding BPSL), up from ~35.7mt current.
Targeting net neutrality in carbon emissions by 2050.
Target to maintain more than 50% share of Value-Added and Special Products (VASP) in total sales; VASP share at 61% in Q3.
Committed to keep net gearing (ND/Equity) within stated cap of 1.75x and leverage (ND/EBITDA) within stated cap of 3.75x; currently 0.92x and 2.91x.
Energy transition: 2.5GW of RE and 320MWh battery storage capacity approved, of which ~1GW capacity commissioned.
Contemplating introduction of an energy surcharge as a separate line item to pass on unsustainable coking coal price increases to customers.
